key_insight: SELDON uses continuous-time deep ODE latent dynamics inside a variational autoencoder to model and forecast supernova light curves, enabling millisecond-scale posterior inference per object compared with hours for legacy MCMC pipelines.
problem_solved: How to perform fast, calibrated inference and forecasting on millions of optical-transient alerts (e.g., from LSST) when traditional physics-based MCMC methods are far too slow to scale.
method: Continuous-time variational autoencoder that models latent evolution with neural ODEs to represent irregularly sampled light curves and their dynamics.
Amortized inference: an encoder maps observed photometry to a posterior over latent ODE initial conditions; the decoder/ODE generates forecasts and parameter posteriors quickly.
Trained on simulated and/or labeled transient light curves to learn a fast surrogate for physical inference while preserving uncertainty quantification.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable surrogate for physical inference that enables real-time classification, parameter estimation, and scheduling for follow-up observations at LSST-scale alert rates.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: streaming alerts → SELDON encoder → latent ODE → fast posterior & forecasts
Time-series panel: observed irregular photometry, reconstructed light curve, and forward forecasts with uncertainty bands
Bar/line chart comparing per-object inference time and throughput (SELDON millisecond vs MCMC hours)
Latent-space visualization (e.g., 2D embedding) showing clustering of supernova types and uncertainty ellipses
paper_title: SELDON: Supernova Explosions Learned by Deep ODE Networks
paper_authors: Jiezhong Wu, Jack O'Brien, Jennifer Li, M. S. Krafczyk, Ved G. Shah
